title: visualize an incident using authorized telemetry sources
input: The operator selects approved data sources, dashboard queries and team viewer permissions.
action: Managed Grafana hosts the configured Grafana workspace and queries its authorized metric or log sources. The panels visualize returned evidence; collection occurs through the source telemetry systems.
output: The on-call team compares errors and latency panels with the incident timeline and investigates the underlying service.
check: Test workspace roles, data freshness, query scope and dashboard behavior when a source is unavailable.

title: process a large research dataset through parallel file access
input: The research owner selects approved source data and compatible compute-to-filesystem connectivity.
action: Managed Lustre provides the configured parallel filesystem for supported compute clients. Workers mount its namespace and run the scientific solver; supported blob integration must be configured for the intended data movement.
output: The compute job publishes completed outputs through the approved storage export or persistence path.
check: Check mount permissions, parallel throughput, source synchronization and recovery of required output files.

title: geocode delivery addresses and display a permitted route
input: The dispatch application submits authorized addresses or coordinates and route constraints.
action: Azure Maps executes the selected supported geographic API, such as geocoding, routing or map rendering. The dispatcher interprets the result and decides the actual delivery assignment.
output: The application displays the reviewed route and approved location data to the assigned driver.
check: Check coordinate conventions, route restrictions, location privacy and the API's current supported version.

title: assess and migrate a supported server estate
input: The migration owner identifies source servers, utilization history and application dependency groups.
action: Azure Migrate's configured assessment and migration tools discover supported sources, estimate target suitability and perform the selected replication or migration workflow. Assessment output informs sizing; application acceptance still requires target testing.
output: The owner runs the migrated application in an isolated Azure target and prepares an approved client cutover.
check: Validate server boot, dependencies, replicated state and final-write coordination before accepting the move.

title: connect approved Azure and partner-cloud network endpoints
input: The network owner specifies supported provider regions, prefixes and redundancy requirements.
action: Multicloud Interconnect supplies the selected supported private connectivity arrangement between Azure and the partner network. Routing and address policy govern reachability; application identity remains with the endpoints.
output: The Azure application connects to the permitted partner-cloud database over the reviewed private path.
check: Test route propagation, return traffic, denied prefixes and failover using the actual provider offering.

title: deploy a supported network function onto edge infrastructure
input: The network operator selects a supported function package and approved edge device configuration.
action: Network Function Manager coordinates supported network-function lifecycle actions on the selected infrastructure. The deployed function processes eligible network traffic; the manager handles deployment and management requests.
output: The operator configures the deployed function's intended traffic path and policies.
check: Check package compatibility, function health, routed traffic and rollback before carrying operational traffic.

title: enrich a demand forecast with an approved public dataset
input: The analyst selects a public dataset version, geography and applicable usage terms.
action: Open Datasets provides access to selected public datasets for analysis and model development. The analysis job reads and joins the chosen records; the dataset offering does not train a demand model automatically.
output: The engineer joins the approved weather or calendar features to internal demand records.
check: Check dates, units, join coverage, licensing and leakage before using the features in training.

title: summarize an authorized support case with a deployed model
input: The support backend submits permitted case text to its configured model deployment.
action: The selected Azure OpenAI deployment generates a response for the submitted prompt under supported model settings. The application controls input scope and validates the generated summary; generation does not establish factual correctness.
output: The support agent reviews the summary against the original case before saving it.
check: Test hallucinations, prompt injection, sensitive-data policy and deployment access using representative cases.

title: host a supported telecom network function on operator infrastructure
input: The operator selects supported Nexus infrastructure, network-function artifacts and network attachment requirements.
action: Operator Nexus supplies the supported telecom-oriented infrastructure platform for deploying the selected workloads. The network function runs on its assigned compute and network resources; operator configuration determines packet treatment.
output: The function serves the configured telecom network path under its separate subscriber and traffic policies.
check: Validate function compatibility, network attachments, capacity and recovery under node or link failure.

title: orchestrate an approved telecom service deployment
input: The operator supplies service definitions, supported network-function artifacts and deployment values.
action: Operator Service Manager coordinates supported service and network-function deployment lifecycles from the configured definitions. Deployed functions perform telecom operations; the manager tracks provisioning and updates.
output: The operator tests the instantiated service and advances rollout only after the network acceptance gate.
check: Check definition versions, permissions, actual function readiness and rollback of a failed deployment.
